# inputs

<!-- Generated by orb-weaver-kicad-board-docs from board.yaml and board-manifest.yaml; do not edit. -->

Subsystem sheet `/inputs` of **camera-gpio-interface-pcb**, from the board recipe `subsystems/inputs.subsystem.yaml`.

The two pyControl BNC inputs, TRIG IN and SYNC IN: each jack into the shared USBLC6 ESD clamp referenced to +5V, then the logic_input_2ch_5v_schmitt_sn74lvc2g17 block, which conditions a 3.3 V or 5 V edge into clean 3.3 V logic (TRIG_IN, SYNC_IN) and taps each for the InstrumentPort; a 680 Ω activity LED on each conditioned output.

Board note: board-authored sheet, 7 parts

## Notes

- J301 is TRIG IN (the 150 Hz frame trigger, to the cameras' Line 3) and J302 is SYNC IN (the Rsync pulse, to Line 0 and to SYNC OUT). Both chains are identical, so reversing the roles is a cable swap plus the cameras' TriggerSource. Shells to ground, no termination footprint.
- U301 (USBLC6-2P6) clamps TRIG_RAW and SYNC_RAW with its VBUS on +5V, so it sits above a 5 V logic high and never conducts on a 3.3 V signal. The block behind it (4.7 kΩ series, 470 pF to ground, 100 kΩ pull-down on the jack side) tolerates a 5 V source or a ±5 V OneBox DAC plugged in by mistake, and an unplugged jack reads low, so the cameras receive nothing rather than noise.
- D301 and D302 through R301 and R302 (680 Ω, about 1.8 mA) show activity on TRIG_IN and SYNC_IN: a 25 ms Rsync pulse once a second blinks, the 150 Hz trigger reads half-lit. The instrument taps TRIG_IN_INST and SYNC_IN_INST are the block's own IN_A_INST and IN_B_INST ports, so the board adds none.
- The conditioning delays a 3.3 V edge about 2 µs, the same on both inputs, so trigger-to-Rsync timing is preserved. TRIG_IN then feeds the three Line 3 drivers and SYNC_IN the three Line 0 drivers and the SYNC OUT driver, through the root.
